## What changed

**Nothing was changed on this task, because the optimizer never saw it.** The N=30 pilot's `val` split contained 2 tasks (`traces_parsec-aap2-0047` and `-0048`); this is one of the other 28. It has exactly one measurement in the whole experiment: a single trial in the reference sweep.

## What worked

The tool sequence. `trajectory: 1.000` — the seed skill reproduced all 3 demanded calls, so it went looking in the right places in the right order.

## What didn't

The answer. Only **1 of 4** `answer_contains` assertions passed (`assertions: 0.250`), capping the reward at **0.625** under the 50/50 weighting.

## What we can (or can't) learn

**That the two halves of v1's reward fail independently, and that the trajectory half is the one the seed skill can already do here.** This task is in the 5-task minority whose demanded sequence was actually callable, so it is one of the few v1 rows where trajectory is not the binding constraint — and where the score says something about the skill rather than about which simulators were running. What binds is getting specific strings into the answer, a different capability from choosing tools and the one an edit to a skill file has the best chance of moving. It was never tested: the optimizer did not run on this task.
